items.note: The display defines B_k, q_k, d_k, t_k, Δ_k, c and asserts q_k > 0, -g_kᵀs_k = α_kq_k and c = 1 - c₂ > 0. notation_display states these with the library names (R.hessian k = (R.H k)⁻¹, R.q k, R.d k := α_k q_k, R.curvature k = y_kᵀs_k); Δ_k and c are written out as F (R.x k) - F (R.x (k + 1)) and 1 - R.c₂. Run = R : AdmissibleBFGSRun n F (the chapter inherits the infinite-admissible-run convention, line 9).
For every k: c₁d_k ≤ Δ_k ≤ d_k, t_k ≥ (1 - c₂)d_k and (1 - c₂)d_k > 0 (the display's "t_k ≥ c d_k > 0"). Same claim as the article's A/energy/disp/004 (part of Lemma art:run-invariants).
B_{k+1} = B_k - g_kg_kᵀ/q_k + y_ky_kᵀ/t_k for every k (outer, total inverse; q_k, t_k > 0).
M_k is the variable M k with its defining equation M k = B_k - q_k⁻¹ g_kg_kᵀ; conclusion: M_k ⪰ 0 (PosSemidef) and M_k s_k = 0.

items.title: A low sublevel is an invariant local basin
items.note: Hypotheses as in the text: F finite convex (ConvexOn ℝ univ F) with unique minimizer x_* (hmin, huniq), positive dimension (1 ≤ n), a specified neighborhood U ∈ 𝓝 x_* and r > 0 with the closed Euclidean ball B̄_r(x_*) ⊆ U; ω_r is the variable ω with ω = sInf of F(x_*+z) - F(x_*) over the Euclidean sphere ‖z‖ = r. Conclusions: the sphere is nonempty; ω_r is attained (IsLeast, the "min" of the display); ω_r > 0; for every x_0 with F(x_0) - F(x_*) < ω_r the sublevel {F ≤ F(x_0)} lies in the open Euclidean ball B_r(x_*); and, for the title's "invariant basin", every admissible run with F(x_0) - F(x_*) < ω_r stays in B_r(x_*) ⊆ U (no assumption on H_0). The library's Localization lemmas are for a general normed space (on Vec n the sup norm); the Euclidean statements are proved here along the text's radial argument. Non-vacuity (example in the module): x²/2 on ℝ¹, x_* = 0, U = ℝ, r = 2 (ω₂ = 2, computed from sphere_min), and the article's quadratic run, which starts with F(x_0) - F(x_*) = 1/2 < ω₂, so the condition of the run-invariance conjunct holds for an actual run.

Undisplayed steps: continuity, compactness of the sphere and uniqueness give ω_r > 0 (sphere_min); Armijo keeps every accepted iterate in the initial sublevel (objective_le_initial, used in localization); no bound on H_0 is assumed and rejected trials are not part of a run; "This argument also proves boundedness of every sublevel ..." and the dimension-zero remark are localization_remarks (every sublevel bounded and compact; for n = 0 all points coincide).
Under the lemma's assumptions (ω_r as in the lemma), for ‖x - x_*‖ ≥ r (Euclidean): F(x) - F(x_*) ≥ (‖x - x_*‖/r)ω_r and (‖x - x_*‖/r)ω_r ≥ ω_r.

items.title: Strict contours give vanishing steps on a positive limiting level
items.note: "The run is contained in a compact sublevel": b with {F ≤ b} compact and F(x_k) ≤ b for all k; "F(x_k) ↓ ℓ": the values are antitone (automatic for admissible runs, hypothesis _hmono unused) and tend to ℓ; F_* = min F is IsLeast (Set.range F) Fstar; ℓ > F_*; "the boundary of {F ≤ ℓ} contains no nontrivial line segment": every segment [x,z] ⊆ frontier {F ≤ ℓ} has x = z. Conclusion s_k → 0 (Tendsto R.displacement atTop (𝓝 0); every norm gives the same topology). Non-vacuity, with a positive limiting level, by an actual failing run of the article's Theorem art:local-failure-lower on its strongly convex objective (example in the module).

The library proof follows this route: d_k → 0 from Armijo; compact consecutive-pair limits x ≠ z; convexity bounds values on the accepted segment above by F(x_k) and the supporting inequality below by F(x_k) - d_k (segment_value_lower), so F = ℓ on [x,z] (cluster_pair_segment_constant); a point with value below ℓ puts the segment in the frontier (level_mem_frontier). The last sentence describes the proof route.

items.title: Principal-minor hierarchy
items.note: Standing assumptions written out as in the article's MatrixAlgebra.lean: hH : H ≻ 0, hs : s = -αHg, hα : α > 0, q = gᵀHg > 0, β = -yᵀHg/q > 0, H₊ = inverseBFGS H s y; ‖y‖² is sqNorm y; e_j is principalSum. The statement does not repeat H ≻ 0 and α > 0: the text defines e_j only for SPD matrices (line 63), so e_j(H) and e_j(H₊) presuppose H, H₊ ≻ 0, which (with q, β > 0, t = αβq) is equivalent to α > 0, and an ordinary update has a positive length (the inherited convention). Not a discrepancy; hierarchy_needs_positive_length shows that the inequality fails for α < 0 when e_j is extended to all matrices (Lean's principalSum). Same claim as the article's Theorem art:minor-hierarchy (A/energy/theorem/art:minor-hierarchy), which states H ≻ 0 and α > 0. Wording point (optional, not a discrepancy): state the assumptions as the article does, e.g. "Let $H\succ0$ and $\alpha>0$. For the inverse-BFGS update with $s=-\alpha Hg$, $q=g^THg>0$ and $\beta=-y^THg/q>0$, ...".

The library's principalMinorHierarchy follows this proof (as for the article's A/energy/proof/003). Undisplayed steps, stated in the article's MatrixAlgebra.lean: κ = gᵀHy = -βq (kappa_eq_and_curvature); the compression formula of line 81 (compression_formula); "All Gram determinants are nonnegative" (gram_dets_nonneg); "only A must be invertible, which it is" (Ch02M.compression_notation); the compressed rank-one step (compression_update); the per-subspace bound (gram_compression); "The rank-one increases sum to at most (α/β)e_j(H)" and the conclusion (principalMinorHierarchy, via eigenbasis_gram_sum and principalGramSumIdentity); "For j = n ... det H₊ = (α/β) det H" (full_dimension_case, det_update). Gram_H(g,y,Z) is read as [g y Z]ᵀH[g y Z].

Verbatim the article's display (H₊ = 𝓕 + α/(βq) vvᵀ) with the same definitions v = Hg, κ = gᵀHy = -βq, P = I - vyᵀ/κ, 𝓕 = PHPᵀ, under the same assumptions (those of Theorem M:hierarchy; the article states H ≻ 0 and α > 0, see the note on C/02_M/theorem/M:hierarchy). Lean: BfgsCoverage.Article.MatrixAlgebra.update_split.

Defines A = ZᵀHZ, a = ZᵀHg, b = ZᵀHy, r = yᵀHy, u = aᵀA⁻¹a, w = aᵀA⁻¹b, z = bᵀA⁻¹b for Z with j orthonormal columns. The theorems of the proof take these as variables with exactly these defining equations (MatrixAlgebra.compression_determinant, gram_schur, ...). compression_notation shows that they are meaningful: A ≻ 0 and A⁻¹ is a two-sided inverse (also the claim "only A must be invertible, which it is", line 103). Unlike the article's display, the companion's does not assert A ≻ 0.
Verbatim the article's equation art:compression-determinant, same notation and assumptions (Lean: MatrixAlgebra.compression_determinant).
The first identity of the article's display, det Gram_H(y,Z) = det A (r - z), same notation (Lean: MatrixAlgebra.gram_schur, first conjunct).
The second identity of the article's display, det Gram_H(g,y,Z) = det A((q-u)(r-z) - (κ-w)²) (Lean: MatrixAlgebra.gram_schur, second conjunct); Gram_H(g,y,Z) = [g y Z]ᵀH[g y Z].
Verbatim the article's display (the companion labels it M:compression); Lean: MatrixAlgebra.compression_gram_bound.

Under the theorem's assumptions, with Z, v, κ, P, 𝓕 (Lean F), A, a, b, r, u as defined: det(ZᵀH₊Z) = det(Zᵀ𝓕Z) + (α/(βq)) det A u (the change is exactly that), (α/(βq)) det A u ≤ (α/β) det A, and u ≤ q.

The article's display with its middle sum omitted (both remaining relations are parts of the article's chain); the companion's E_I (coordinate j-subsets of an orthonormal eigenbasis) is the article's Z_I, y_i the coordinates of y in that basis. Lean: Energy.eigenbasis_gram_sum.

items.title: Bounded gradients and vanishing predicted decrease
items.note: "An infinite full-BFGS run ... fixed weak Wolfe": under the chapter's convention an admissible run (average; its weak-Wolfe constant c₂ < 1 is fixed). average_full_bfgs proves the same for every full-BFGS sequence (H₀ ≻ 0, g_k ≠ 0, α_k > 0, the inverse update) satisfying weak Wolfe with a fixed 0 < c₂ < 1, with no objective. Bounded gradients: ∃ Λ, ∀ k, ‖g_k‖ ≤ Λ (Euclidean); d_k → 0: Tendsto R.d atTop (𝓝 0); the limits are stated as written (real power 1/N; (1/N)∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹). Same claim as the article's Theorem art:reciprocal-growth.

Same proof as the article's A/energy/proof/004 (G = Λ, c = ω); the library proves it in logarithmic form. Undisplayed steps: β_k ≥ c and ‖y_k‖ ≤ 2G (Energy.run_bounds); "Multiplying and summing yields V_η(H_{k+1}) ≤ (2η/q_k)V_η(H_k), while q_k ≤ G²V_η(H_k)" (Energy.potential_contraction, Ch02M.q_le_potential); arithmetic-geometric mean (logMean_le_arithmeticMean).

Standing assumptions: those of the theorem, G > 0 with ‖g_k‖ ≤ G for all k, K₀ = 4G²/c² (c = 1 - c₂). For every k and 1 ≤ j ≤ n: e_j(H_{k+1}) ≤ q_k⁻¹(K₀e_{j+1}(H_k) + (d_k/c)e_j(H_k)) (the article's display A/energy/disp/018 multiplied out).
Adds η > 0 and J with d_k/c ≤ η for k ≥ J; V_η is the variable V with V H = ∑_{j=1}^n (K₀/η)^{j-1} e_j(H) for SPD H (Finset.Icc 1 n). The claim is V_η(H) ≥ tr H for every SPD H.

The product bound of the article's display (its second part), with Λ = G and ω = c and the same standing assumptions (G > 0, ‖g_k‖ ≤ G, K₀ = 4G²/c², η > 0, d_k/c ≤ η for k ≥ J, V_η); m ≥ 1 is implicit (Lean: Energy.potential_contraction).

items.title: Finite horizon and superquadratic growth under summability
items.note: "Assume bounded gradients": a bound G > 0 with ‖g_k‖ ≤ G for all k (Euclidean); fixed weak Wolfe: the run's c₂ < 1, c = 1 - c₂; ∑d_k < ∞: Summable R.d. G, K₀ and V_η appear in (M:finitehorizon) but are defined only in the proof of Theorem M:average: K₀ = 4G²/c² and V_η(H) = ∑_{j=1}^n (K₀/η)^{j-1}e_j(H) (the variable V η H, for η > 0 and SPD H). The claim holds for every gradient bound G > 0 (the Lean statement quantifies over all of them), so the truth value is unaffected. Wording point (not a discrepancy): proposed "with $G$, $K_0=4G^2/c^2$ and $V_\eta$ as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{M:average}". Conclusions: D_J = ∑_{k≥J} d_k > 0; for every η > 0 and m ≥ 2 the bound (M:finitehorizon) with real powers and the sum over Finset.Ico J (J + m); (1/N²)∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ → ∞. superquadratic_full_bfgs proves all three conclusions (D_J > 0 included) for full-BFGS sequences with weak Wolfe (no objective). The article cites both consequences (A/energy/prose/022).

Undisplayed steps: arithmetic-geometric mean for the reciprocals (reciprocal_sum_ge_exp, hierarchy_finite_horizon_rpow); "With J fixed, V_η(H_J) grows at most polynomially in m, of degree n-1. Its mth root tends to one" for η = D_J/[c(m-1)] (SharpPotentialDegree.run_optimized_bound, potentialPolynomial_natDegree, run_optimized_root_tendsto, sharpPrincipalPotential); the fixed prefix and J → ∞ (hierarchy_superquadratic_growth). "No uniform bound on H_J as J varies is used" is visible in the statements (no such hypothesis).
Under the theorem's assumptions and the given η > 0, m ≥ 2: V_η(H_{k+1}) ≤ ((η + d_k/c)/q_k) V_η(H_k) for every k (no tail restriction).

Both inequalities for the given η > 0 and m ≥ 2: ∏_{k=J}^{J+m-1} q_k ≤ G²V_η(H_J)∏_{k=J}^{J+m-2} (η + d_k/c) ≤ G²V_η(H_J)(η + D_J/(c(m-1)))^{m-1} (products over Finset.Ico; the first by iterating display disp/022 and the endpoint bound q ≤ G²V_η, the second by arithmetic-geometric mean).

With the tail J fixed and D_J = ∑_{k≥J} d_k: liminf_{N→∞} N⁻²∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ ≥ c/(2D_J), stated as (i) every a < c/(2D_J) is eventually ≤ N⁻²∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ and (ii) the liminf in EReal is ≥ c/(2D_J) (a real-valued liminf is not used: the sequence is unbounded). Proved along the text's route (η = D_J/[c(m-1)], polynomial potential) by the library's hierarchy_fixed_tail_lower_eventually.

R_k = (y_kᵀr_{k+1})²/t_k (variable Rk, R names the run) is the library's referenceCorrection; reference_notation unfolds r_k, a_k, E_k, R_k to the library definitions. Same notation as the article's A/energy/disp/006.
For any fixed x_* and every k: r_{k+1} = r_k - α_kH_kg_k (the expansion point named in the lead-in, prose/015) and E_{k+1} = E_k - a_k²/q_k + R_k (as the article's A/energy/disp/007).
x_* a minimizer (∀ z, F x_* ≤ F z), F_* = F(x_*); for every N: [F(x_N) - F_*]²∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ ≤ E_0 + ∑_{k<N} R_k (as the article's A/energy/disp/008).
The supposition V_{k+1} = V_kT_k + s_kb_kᵀ (frames V_k ∈ ℝ^{n×r}) is hypothesis hV of frame_identity (EnergyIdentities.rectOuter s b is s bᵀ).

Under the supposition of disp/028, with A_k = V_kᵀB_kV_k, a_k = V_kᵀg_k, c_k = V_{k+1}ᵀy_k (variables with defining equations; c_k is unrelated to c = 1 - c₂): for every k, A_{k+1} = T_kᵀ(A_k - a_ka_kᵀ/q_k)T_k + c_kc_kᵀ/t_k. Frames may be rectangular and rank deficient.

Stated under the suppositions of line 204 (prose/022): a tail J; ‖a_k‖ ≥ ε > 0 and ‖c_k‖²/t_k ≤ C for k ≥ J (unused); P_J = I (unused), P_{k+1} = P_kT_k for k ≥ J; bounded norms ∃ K, ‖P_k‖_op ≤ K (unused) and bounded inverse norms: P_k invertible (det ≠ 0) and ∃ L, ‖P_k⁻¹‖_op ≤ L (unused), Euclidean operator norms. Ã_k = P_k^{-T}A_kP_k^{-1} (variable At, ((P k)⁻¹)ᵀ for P_k^{-T}). Conclusion for every k ≥ J. Proved from normalized_trace_step (one step: V_{k+1} = V_kT_k + s_kb_kᵀ, P_k, P_{k+1} invertible, P_{k+1} = P_kT_k). The full suppositions are satisfiable (example in the module, logRun: n = 1, F(x) = 1 - x for x ≤ 1 and -log x for x ≥ 1, x_k = 2^{k+1}, H_k = x_k²/2, α_k = 2, (c₁,c₂) = (1/4,1/2); frames V_k = [x_k], T_k = 1, b_k = 1, P_k = 1, J = 0, ε = 1, C = 2; bounded gradients and d_k = 1); they cannot hold together with bounded gradients and d_k → 0 (frame_criterion).

items.title: Residuals in fixed smooth directions
items.note: Bounded gradients (∃ Λ, ∀ k, ‖g_k‖ ≤ Λ), fixed weak Wolfe (the run), ∑d_k < ∞ (Summable R.d); a fixed subspace S of Euclidean ℝⁿ (Submodule of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) with P_S its orthogonal projection (S.orthogonalProjection); ‖P_Sy_k‖² ≤ L_St_k for all k (the library needs it only on the tail). Conclusion: no J, width p, frames V_k ∈ ℝ^{n×p}, T_k, b_k, residuals R_k (Rres) and constants m, C₀, C_T, C_R (arbitrary reals) with m > 0 and, for all k ≥ J, ‖V_kᵀg_k‖² ≥ m, ‖V_{k+1}ᵀy_k‖² ≤ C₀t_k, V_{k+1} = V_kT_k + s_kb_kᵀ + R_k, ‖T_k‖²_op ≤ 1 + C_Td_k (Euclidean operator norm, FrameNorms.euclideanOpNorm), range R_k ⊆ S (every R_k v ∈ S), ‖R_k‖_F² ≤ C_Rd_k (SmoothSubspace.frobSq, the sum of squared entries). "No full-rank frame or invertible transport is required": the statement has no such hypothesis. The library represents S by an orthonormal basis matrix U with P_S = UUᵀ (orthogonalProjection_eq, projection_basis, range_projection connect the two forms).

The library proof follows this route (residual_frame_step, residual_frames_incompatible). Undisplayed steps: "Consequently tr(P_SB_k) ≤ C_S + L_Sk", derived not imposed (smooth_subspace_projection_trace_bound; C_S = tr(P_SB_0)); the real factor C_k with M_k = C_kᵀC_k and the entrywise Young inequality (gram_trace_square, scalar_young, gram_trace_add_le); "The parenthesized energy is nonnegative" (second conclusion of Ch02M.frame_young_step; frame_descent_nonneg); "Finite ∑d_k gives 1 ≤ P_k ≤ P̄ < ∞" (Energy.normalization_bounds, with P̄ = exp(C₁∑_{j≥J}d_j)); "contrary to Theorem M:superquadratic" (residual_recurrence_incompatible). The displays are proof-by-contradiction displays: see the notes on disp/035-disp/040.

Standing assumptions: the theorem's hypotheses and the frames on the tail J that the proof assumes (unused here), and P_S as a matrix PS of the orthogonal projection (hPS). For every k: tr(P_SB_{k+1}) = tr(P_SB_k) - ‖P_Sg_k‖²/q_k + ‖P_Sy_k‖²/t_k ≤ tr(P_SB_k) + L_S. The standing assumptions of the proof cannot all hold (that is the theorem); the general form projection_trace_step (one k, only ‖P_Sy_k‖² ≤ L_St_k) has satisfiable assumptions.

Adds E_k = tr(V_kᵀB_kV_k) and M_k of (M:annihilation) (variables). For every k ≥ J: E_{k+1} = tr[(V_kT_k + R_k)ᵀM_k(V_kT_k + R_k)] + ‖V_{k+1}ᵀy_k‖²/t_k. General form frame_energy_step (one k, only the frame relation at k).

For every k ≥ J: E_{k+1} ≤ (1+d_k)‖T_k‖²(E_k - ‖V_kᵀg_k‖²/q_k) + (1+d_k⁻¹)tr(R_kᵀM_kR_k) + C₀, ‖T_k‖ the Euclidean operator norm. General form frame_young_step (one k: frame relation and ‖V_{k+1}ᵀy_k‖² ≤ C₀t_k), which also states that the parenthesized energy is nonnegative.

Adds C_S = tr(P_SB_0) (the constant of the derived bound tr(P_SB_k) ≤ C_S + L_Sk). For every k ≥ J: tr(R_kᵀM_kR_k) ≤ ‖R_k‖_F² tr(P_SB_k) ≤ C_Rd_k(C_S + L_Sk). General form residual_energy_step (one k: range R_k ⊆ S, ‖R_k‖_F² ≤ C_Rd_k, the smoothness bound for all k).

"On a tail with d_k ≤ 1" (the text keeps the name J; hypothesis d_k ≤ 1 for k ≥ J): there are C₁, C₂ ≥ 0 with E_{k+1} ≤ (1 + C₁d_k)(E_k - m/q_k) + C₂(k+1) for every k ≥ J. The text leaves C₁, C₂ unspecified; the proof takes C₁ = 1 + 2max(C_T,0), C₂ = 2C_R(C_S + L_S) + C₀ (residual_recurrence_step, the general form at one k with explicit constants).

Adds the conclusion of disp/039 (C₁, C₂ ≥ 0 and the recurrence on the tail), P_{k+1} = P_k(1 + C₁d_k) with P_J = 1, and P̄ with P_k ≤ P̄ for k ≥ J (such P̄ exists by finite ∑d_k: Energy.normalization_bounds). For every N ≥ J: (m/P̄)∑_{k=J}^{N-1} q_k⁻¹ ≤ E_J + C₂∑_{k=J}^{N-1}(k+1), and the right side is O(N²) (Asymptotics.IsBigO). The scalar step is normalized_budget.

items.anchor: A finite convex function has uniformly bounded subgradients on any compact set $K$.
items.note: ∃ G, ∀ x ∈ K, every subgradient g of F at x (∀ y, gᵀ(y-x) ≤ F(y) - F(x)) has ‖g‖ ≤ G (Euclidean). Used in the chapter (and the library) to bound gradients on compact sublevels.

items.anchor: Indeed, choose $\epsilon>0$ and bound its continuous values on $K+\epsilon\overline B$.
items.note: The two sentences of the argument: for ε > 0 there are M (bound of F on K + εB̄, compact) and m (lower bound on K) with gᵀu ≤ (M - m)/ε for every subgradient g at x ∈ K and every Euclidean unit u, hence ‖g‖ ≤ (M - m)/ε.

items.anchor: This does not require differentiability throughout $K$.
items.note: The bound of prose/007 concerns every supporting vector at every point of K and has no differentiability hypothesis.

items.anchor: For SPD $H$, let $e_j(H)$ be the elementary symmetric polynomial of degree $j$ of its eigenvalues
items.note: Lean's e_j(H) is principalSum H j (sum of the j×j principal minors, defined for every matrix); elementary_symmetric_def proves that for SPD H it equals the j-th elementary symmetric polynomial of the eigenvalues (Multiset.esymm of hH.isHermitian.eigenvalues, with multiplicity) for every j, and e_{n+1}(H) = 0.

items.anchor: Thus $e_1=\operatorname{tr}$ and $e_n=\det$.
items.note: For SPD H: e_1(H) = tr H and e_n(H) = det H.

items.anchor: These conclusions do not say $H_k\to0$, $q_k\to0$ pointwise, or that eigenvectors converge.

items.anchor: Thus $\sum_{k<N}R_k=o(\sum_{k<N}q_k^{-1})$ excludes a positive gap.
items.note: "Thus ∑_{k<N}R_k = o(∑_{k<N}q_k⁻¹) excludes a positive gap": with x_* a minimizer, F_* = F(x_*) and the o(·) as Asymptotics.IsLittleO, F(x_k) → F_* (no gap ≥ η > 0 persists). The deduction from (M:energybound) needs ∑_{k<N}q_k⁻¹ → ∞ (negligible_corrections_of_divergent assumes exactly that); the sentence leaves the hypothesis giving it implicit: Theorem M:average supplies it under bounded gradients (d_k → 0 follows from the minimizer), and negligible_corrections assumes bounded gradients, as the library's objective_tendsto_min_of_negligible_corrections. Without bounded gradients the claim is not proved here, but no counterexample is known (R_k = 0 for all k and ∑q_k⁻¹ < ∞ would be needed; impossible in one dimension), and "Thus" points correctly back to (M:energybound), so this is the article's A/energy/prose/010 situation, not a discrepancy (the secondary aspect of M10, without its wrong reference). Wording point (not a discrepancy): proposed "Thus, along runs with bounded gradients, $\sum_{k<N}R_k=o(\sum_{k<N}q_k^{-1})$ excludes a positive gap."

items.anchor: With the summability assumptions of Theorem~\ref{M:superquadratic}, an $O(N^2)$ cumulative correction suffices.
items.note: Bounded gradients and Summable R.d (the assumptions of Theorem M:superquadratic), x_* a minimizer, F_* = F(x_*): if ∑_{k<N}R_k = O(N²) (Asymptotics.IsBigO), then F(x_k) → F_* (no positive gap). The library's QuadraticCorrectionTarget proves the same with a unique minimizer instead of bounded gradients.

items.anchor: Suppose on a hypothetical nonoptimal tail
items.note: The suppositions of the moving-frame criterion (‖a_k‖ ≥ ε > 0, ‖c_k‖²/t_k ≤ C, P_J = I, P_{k+1} = P_kT_k with bounded norms and bounded inverse norms) are the hypotheses of frame_criterion and normalized_trace; "Congruence by P_{k+1}^{-1} and a trace yield" is the lead-in of disp/030. "Nonoptimal" is descriptive, not a hypothesis of the Lean statements (frame_criterion, normalized_trace), which are therefore more general; the suppositions are satisfiable (example logRun in the module, whose values tend to inf F = -∞).

items.anchor: Positivity gives $\sum_{J\le k<N}q_k^{-1}=O(N)$, contradicting Theorem~\ref{M:average}.
items.note: Under the suppositions of prose/022 (frames V_{k+1} = V_kT_k + s_kb_kᵀ, Euclidean operator norms): ∑_{J≤k<N} q_k⁻¹ = O(N) (IsBigO), and the suppositions cannot hold together with the hypotheses of Theorem M:average (bounded gradients and d_k → 0), which is the contradiction. The paragraph does not restate those hypotheses; "contradicting Theorem M:average" refers to them (a correct reference). Non-vacuity of the O(N) part: the suppositions are satisfiable (example logRun in the module: bounded gradients, d_k = 1, ∑_{J≤k<N} q_k⁻¹ = 2(N - J)), so the hypotheses of Theorem M:average are really needed for the contradiction; logRun's values tend to inf F = -∞, so it is not a nonoptimal tail and does not refute the sentence. Wording point (optional, not a discrepancy): "..., contradicting Theorem~\ref{M:average} when the gradients are bounded ($d_k\to0$ holds on a nonoptimal tail of a bounded-below objective)".
